subject: Renewal ladder: cliffless top-up + one-time onboarding credit
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma@tritonhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Triton Procurement <procurement@tritonhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal options — cliffless top-up + credit?

Hi Karthik / Ben,

We're starting renewal planning for Triton's Q4 and projecting a ~45% workload increase driven by two pilots that will move to production next quarter. Our finance team asked if Redwood can offer a top-up path that doesn't have the usual "cliff" (i.e., avoid a big discrete commit step) and instead allow staged increases with protective true-up terms.

Separately, we'd like to discuss a one-time onboarding credit to cover integration work we need from Redwood Professional Services — that would let us accelerate the pilots.

Attached is our current contract and Q2 usage for reference. Can you outline a few commercial options (pricing ladder, pro-rate behavior, shortfall protections) and an indicative number for a one-time onboarding credit?

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Li
Head of Platform Engineering
Triton Health

Attachments: Triton_current_contract_Q3.pdf, usage_report_q2.csv

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@tritonhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal options — cliffless top-up + credit?

Emma — thanks for the context and the usage files. High-level, we can do both: a "cliffless" commit ladder and a one-time onboarding credit. Quick sketch below (we'll follow up with a formal quote):

- Cliffless ladder (recommended):
  - Baseline renewal commit (annualized) + three staged top-up buckets you can trigger without renegotiating the whole contract.
  - Unit price steps decline at 25% / 50% / 75% incremental volume bands. No "hard cliff" — shortfall protection is handled via a quarterly true-up with a capped shortfall fee (2% of committed value) instead of immediate charge.

- One-time onboarding credit:
  - $20,000 Professional Services credit to offset integration and training (one-time, to be applied within first 90 days after amendment execution).

- Co-terming option: we can align the staged ladder to your existing renewal date (co-term) so future consumption synchronizes to a single annual renewal.

Open questions for us to price precisely: backlog of queued requests on your end, expected token growth curve, and whether the pilots are latency-sensitive (affects model tier). If you can confirm pilot launch windows, I'll pull numbers.

If helpful, Ben and I can run a quick pricing model on a call — are you available Thursday?

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Director, Revenue — Redwood Inference

Emma — quick commercial note from my side:

- We can model the ladder as 4 internal "reserve slots" (small, medium, large, xlarge). Triton purchases baseline + any number of slots at execution. When actual usage crosses a slot threshold, we auto-apply the priced band and issue a credit if you drop back below at the quarter boundary. This avoids monthly administrative friction.

- I attached a proposed amendment (v1) that shows the ladder language and the 90-day onboarding credit. I'm comfortable starting with a $20k credit but we can flex if you need more PS assistance.

- For procurement: we'll include a clause for a one-time invoice hold / 60-day net on the first invoice after amendment execution as a concession to your finance team. It can be removed after the first renewal if you prefer normal net terms.

I'll also add a DocuSign-ready SOW link once you validate the sizes.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Head of Commercial, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed_amendment_v1.pdf

From: Emma Li <emma@tritonhealth.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 08:54:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal options — cliffless top-up + credit?

Thanks Ben/Karthik. A couple of follow-ups from procurement and finance:

- They want explicit shortfall protection language that caps our downside if pilots underperform. The 2% cap you mentioned is a good start — can we make that explicit in the amendment and add an annual true-up window?

- For the onboarding credit: 90 days is fine, but Procurement would like the credit to be invoiced as a negative line item on the first post-amendment invoice rather than applied as an internal ledger entry.

- SLA credits: we need to ensure standard SLAs carry through the ladder tiers and that any SLA-based credits don't count against the onboarding credit.

We're generally aligned on the ladder concept but need that tightened in the doc. Can you send a revision with the shortfall cap language, invoice mechanics for the credit, and SLA carve-outs? Also please include a redline-ready DocuSign link so Procurement can route for approval.

Best,
Emma

Emma — attached is a revised commercial packet based on your notes: quote_v3.pdf (shows ladder bands and explicit 2% shortfall cap), proposed amendment with invoice mechanics, and a DocuSign-ready SOW link. High level:

- Shortfall protection: 2% cap on committed value per year, with a single annual true-up reconciliation (we agreed).
- Onboarding credit: shown as a negative line item on first invoice after amendment execution; applies only to PS line items (not to SLA credits).
- SLA carve-out: SLA credits are outside of onboarding credit calculation and will be documented in the amendment.

Next steps:
1) Procurement reviews the redlined amendment (DocuSign link included).
2) If ok, sign amendment and we apply the $20k credit and activate the reserve slot structure.
3) Ben will schedule the pricing-model walkthrough and Marissa will coordinate handoff to CS for the onboarding plan.

Are you available tomorrow morning for a 30-min call to walk Procurement through the amendment language?

Thanks — we'll stand by to turn the SOW on submit.
